newsitem.title: CANADA: British woman dies after Canadian cable car crash.
newsitem.headline: British woman dies after Canadian cable car crash.

text.p: A 47-year-old British woman from London died overnight after a funicular railway passenger car crashed in historic Quebec City on Saturday, Quebec City police said on Sunday.
The tourist died after sustaining internal injuries, a broken limb and other injuries to her arms and legs, said Celyne Cantin, Quebec City police spokeswoman.
Her name will not be released until Monday, giving police an opportunity to contact her relatives, Cantin said.

The cable car, which spans part of the former garrison city, fell from a height of 20-25 feet (6-7 metres), injuring 16 tourists from Britain, the United States and the French islands of St. Pierre and Miquelon which are off the east coast of Canada.
None of the other tourists has been released yet from local hospitals, Cantin said. "There is still one in critical condition," she added.

The year-round funicular railway descends from the Chateau Frontenac hotel high above the St. Lawrence river to a lower part of the garrison city. At about 1550 EST (1950 GMT) on Saturday a cable snapped, hurtling the car against a wall of a booth and shattering the windows with the 16 tourists still inside.
